items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: I liked Kate Smith better than anybody, you know. I thought her voice was so beautiful, you see. And I could actually sing just like her, you know.

ctx.x: -- along with your mother when she went to her classes?

No, no, that was after we came -- left Fitzgerald, Georgia. See, this was in Atlanta, Georgia, which was a city. It was called the Little New York City, I mean at that time, but it was still Atlanta. And so they asked me what kind of singing did I do. So I -- luckily I could say that I sang like some famous people at that time, like Mort Downey. He was very famous. And another I did, like a little Paul Robeson, you know, but as a child, you see, I could do bass voice like a little bit. And it's kind of, you know,…

So I told them I sang like Kate Smith, you know, and this 'When the Moon Comes Over the Mountain' and so on. So anyhow I was chosen for the 'Children's Hour', right? So now, once the -- that's the American Broadcasting Company.
